verdict.summary: You can create a Slack app and connect your own workspace in minutes. Turning on Public Distribution (unlisted) needs no review and lets any workspace with your link install the app. However, unlisted apps get much lower conversations.history rate limits, some workspaces block them, and Slack's policy says commercial distribution must go through the Slack Marketplace. The Marketplace requires 10 active workspace installs before you can submit, and review can take up to 10 business days plus up to 10 weeks.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for an unlisted app; 2-5 days to prepare a Marketplace submission (privacy policy, landing/support pages, scope reasons, demo video, test accounts)
verdict.approval_wait: None for dev-workspace or unlisted installs. Marketplace: up to 10 business days (preliminary) plus up to 10 weeks (functional) for new submissions

gates.name: Development workspace (undistributed app)
gates.unlocks: Install and authorize the app in the workspace you created it in, using the full range of app capabilities.
limits: Works only in the workspace the app was created in; other workspaces get invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app
Authorization codes expire after 10 minutes; tokens do not expire unless revoked (or token rotation is on)

gates.name: Public Distribution (unlisted app)
gates.unlocks: Any workspace with your Add to Slack button or install URL can install the app. Not listed in the Marketplace and not reviewed.
limits: All redirect, interactivity and Events API URLs must use HTTPS
conversations.history and conversations.replies limited to 1 request/min and 15 objects per call for non-Marketplace apps (when this applies to existing installs is unclear)
Workspaces with app approval turned on need an admin to approve the app; some workspaces only allow Marketplace-listed apps
Slack treats unlisted apps as a development/testing channel; commercial distribution must go through the Marketplace
No documented cap on the number of installs
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes after the Manage Distribution checklist is complete (takes effect immediately)

gates.name: Slack Marketplace listing
gates.unlocks: Listed in the Slack Marketplace, allowed for commercial distribution, standard rate limits, installable in Marketplace-only workspaces.
limits: At least 10 active workspace installs (used in the past 28 days), kept for the whole review
Each resubmission during preliminary review resets your place in the queue
Review cannot be sped up for launch dates
After publication, scope or redirect URI changes must be resubmitted and approved
gates.time_to_reach: Weeks to months: first reach 10 active workspaces, then up to 10 business days preliminary review plus up to 10 weeks functional review

steps.title: Sign in and create the Slack app
steps.detail: Go to api.slack.com/apps, sign in with your Slack account, and create a new app tied to a development workspace you control. This workspace is the only one where the app can be installed until you turn on distribution.
gotchas: Pick your development workspace carefully: undistributed apps fail with invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app anywhere else.

steps.title: Choose a minimal scope list
steps.detail: Start from the Composio default scopes and keep only the ones your agent uses. Set them under OAuth & Permissions, or in the manifest under oauth_config.scopes (bot / user lists). Bot scopes go in scope= and user scopes go in user_scope=. Drop search:read.*, *:history and files:read unless a feature needs them.
gotchas: Adding scopes later means existing workspaces must reinstall. Removing a scope does not take it off tokens already issued.
Optional scopes in a manifest must also appear in the bot or user list.

steps.title: Add the Redirect URL
steps.detail: In App Management > OAuth & Permissions, add the Composio callback URL as a Redirect URL. It must be HTTPS and contain no fragment, and the redirect_uri sent at authorize time must match it or be a subdirectory of it.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: If you configure several Redirect URLs, send the same redirect_uri in both the authorize and token steps, or Slack returns bad_redirect_uri.

steps.title: Copy credentials into a Composio auth config
steps.detail: From Basic Information, copy the Client ID and Client Secret into a custom Slack auth config in Composio, and enter the same scopes you set in Slack. The endpoints are https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize and https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access.
gotchas: Never put the Client Secret or tokens in client-side code or a public repo.

steps.title: Run a test authorization in your dev workspace
steps.detail: Start a connection through Composio and approve it in your development workspace. Then confirm a bot (and user, if requested) token comes back and that a simple call such as chat:write works.
gotchas: Authorization codes expire after 10 minutes. Finish the exchange promptly.

steps.title: Decide on token rotation and PKCE
steps.detail: Slack tokens do not expire by default. If you want expiring access tokens plus refresh tokens, turn on token rotation; it applies only to newly issued tokens. PKCE can be enabled with oauth_config.pkce_enabled but cannot be turned off afterwards, so check that your Composio setup supports it first.
gotchas: Once PKCE is enabled it cannot be disabled.

steps.title: Activate Public Distribution
steps.detail: In the app dashboard, open Manage Distribution, complete every checklist item (including HTTPS for all redirect and request URLs), and click Activate Public Distribution. This takes effect immediately with no review, and you get an Add to Slack button and a shareable install URL.
gotchas: Unlisted apps get 1 req/min and 15 objects per call on conversations.history and conversations.replies.
Workspaces that require admin approval or allow only Marketplace apps may block the install.

steps.title: Test install on a second workspace
steps.detail: Install the app through the share URL on a workspace other than your development one, and test the uninstall too. If you see invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app, distribution is not active yet.
gotchas: If your agent reads message history, measure conversations.history throughput on this live install to see which rate limit applies.

steps.title: Prepare Marketplace pages and assets
steps.detail: Draft a public landing page with an Add to Slack path and a post-install page, a public privacy policy (data collected, use, retention, contact), and a support page with contact that needs no other account. Also prepare listing assets: a short description of 10 words or fewer, a long description, an icon, 1600x1000 screenshots under 2MB, and a 30-90 second captioned public YouTube demo.
gotchas: You must answer support requests within 2 business days.

steps.title: Write scope reasons and meet policy requirements
steps.detail: Write a reason for each scope that ties it to a feature reviewers can test, and remove scopes meant for future features. Automation-platform apps must request team.billing:read and limit installs to paid-plan workspaces. On free workspaces, the app must not expose message or file data older than 90 days.
gotchas: search:read, admin.* and identity.* are treated as unsuitable. *:history, search:read.* and files:read trigger enhanced review.

steps.title: Reach 10 active workspace installs
steps.detail: Get your unlisted app installed and used on at least 10 workspaces (active means used in the past 28 days). You cannot submit until you reach this, and you must stay at 10 or more for the whole review.
gotchas: Some older pages say 5 workspaces. The current figure is 10; check the submission page in app settings.

steps.title: Submit to the Slack Marketplace
steps.detail: Submit from your app settings. Include a production-ready app tested on a non-development workspace, reviewer test accounts with dummy data, a demo video of the install and OAuth flow, and a way for reviewers to install the app (Slack will not use your testing workspaces).
gotchas: Apps built only for internal use are not suitable for listing.

steps.title: Wait for preliminary and functional review
steps.detail: Preliminary review (listing, scope reasons, installability) usually returns feedback within 10 business days. Functional review, where a reviewer installs and tests the app, takes up to 10 weeks for new submissions. Plan for this ahead of any launch date.
gotchas: Resubmitting during preliminary review resets your place in the queue.

steps.title: Handle post-publication changes through review
steps.detail: After you are listed, changes to scopes or redirect URIs must be resubmitted and approved. New scopes need a staging app and a demo video, and users must reinstall to get them. Requesting unapproved scopes in production causes unapproved_scope errors at install.
gotchas: Changing the Composio callback URL after listing counts as a redirect URI change and needs re-approval.

requirements.item: Slack account and a development workspace
requirements.detail: You must sign in to a Slack account to create an app. No paid plan or org-admin requirement was shown.

requirements.item: HTTPS redirect URL with no fragment
requirements.detail: The redirect_uri must match or be a subdirectory of a configured Redirect URL.
Distributed apps need HTTPS for OAuth redirect, interactivity and Events API URLs.
Needed before you can submit, and must be kept through the whole review.

requirements.item: Public landing page, post-install page and privacy policy
requirements.detail: The privacy policy must state what data is collected, how it is used and retained, and give a contact email or form.

requirements.item: Public support page with a 2-business-day response
requirements.detail: Contacting support must not require another account.
Short description (10 words or fewer), long description, icon, 1600x1000 screenshots under 2MB, 30-90s captioned YouTube demo, pricing model.

requirements.item: Scope reasons, test accounts and install/OAuth demo video
requirements.detail: Each scope must be tied to a testable feature. Provide reviewer accounts with dummy data.

requirements.item: Real customers and a fully built app
requirements.detail: Apps built only for internal use are not suitable for listing.
Request team.billing:read, check the workspace plan after authorization, and never expose the API token to end users.
Do not expose message or file data older than 90 days on free workspaces.

scopes.effect: Allowed by default in workspace governance. No extra scrutiny.
Triggers enhanced Marketplace review. Unlisted apps are also limited to 1 req/min on conversations.history. Workspace admins may require approval.

scopes.scope: search:read.* (public, private, im, mpim, files, users)
scopes.effect: Triggers enhanced Marketplace review. Needs a clear use case such as real-time search or MCP.
Listed as unsuitable for Marketplace apps. Remove it from a self-owned app's scope list.
As user-token scopes they trigger enhanced review. User scopes are accepted only when the app acts as the authenticating user.
Install must be started by an Enterprise org admin or owner at org level. Unlikely to be approved for non-partner Marketplace apps.
Unsuitable for Marketplace apps. For Sign in with Slack, use the OIDC scopes openid/profile/email instead.
Required for automation-platform apps to limit installs to paid-plan workspaces.

blockers.cause: The app is installed on a workspace other than its development workspace before distribution is turned on.
blockers.fix: Complete the Manage Distribution checklist and click Activate Public Distribution.

blockers.cause: Several Redirect URLs are configured and redirect_uri differs between the authorize and token steps, or it doesn't match a configured URL.
blockers.fix: Register the exact Composio callback URL under OAuth & Permissions and send it identically in both steps.

blockers.cause: A published app requests scopes that are not yet approved, either still in review or never submitted.
blockers.fix: Request only approved scopes, or resubmit the new scopes and wait for approval.

blockers.symptom: conversations.history returns only 15 messages and is rate limited to 1 request/min
blockers.fix: Get listed in the Marketplace, or design around the limit. Test on a live install to see whether it applies to you.

blockers.symptom: Install blocked or pending in a customer's workspace
blockers.cause: The workspace requires admin approval for apps or allows only Marketplace-listed apps.
blockers.fix: Ask the workspace admin to approve the app, or get it listed in the Marketplace.
Grow to 10+ workspaces active in the last 28 days and stay there through the review.

blockers.cause: Broad or unnecessary scopes (search:read, admin.*, unneeded user scopes, scopes for future features).
blockers.fix: Trim scopes and give a testable reason for each one.

blockers.symptom: Commercial launch on an unlisted app is not allowed under policy
blockers.cause: The developer policy requires commercially distributed apps to be submitted to the Marketplace.
blockers.fix: Plan for Marketplace review several weeks before a commercial launch.

composio.note: Composio's managed Slack app is fine for testing and internal use. Move to your own app when you need your own branding on the consent screen, a narrower scope list, or a Marketplace listing for commercial distribution (with higher rate limits). Composio's default scopes are broad (search:read, search:read.*, *:history, files:read), and these trigger enhanced or unsuitable-scope handling in Marketplace review, so trim them in your own app. Register the Composio callback URL as the HTTPS Redirect URL under OAuth & Permissions. Endpoints: https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize and https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access.

open_questions: No documented cap on how many workspaces an unlisted (Public Distribution) app can be installed on was found.
Whether existing unlisted installs are already subject to the 1 req/min conversations.history limit is unclear across Slack's pages (March 3, 2026 per one FAQ). Test on a live install.
Prerequisites beyond a Slack sign-in (Developer Program membership, business verification) were not confirmed. Partner-program requirements for admin scopes were not documented.
No single official list of restricted vs. sensitive scopes was found. The tiers here are based on the Marketplace guideline examples.
The Marketplace threshold appears as both 10 and 5 in different snippets. Current pages say 10; confirm on the submission page in app settings.
Review timelines may vary with volume. The actual turnaround is shown on the submission page.
Whether Composio's custom auth config supports Slack PKCE was not verified.
